question: What key administrative change did the Regulating Act introduce for the Governor of Bengal?

options.text: Required direct reporting to the British monarch
Upgraded the post to Governor-General assisted by a council
Shifted administrative control to Madras Presidency

solution:
The correct answer is __**Upgraded the post to Governor-General assisted by a council**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first significant legislative measure by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• The Act marked a key administrative change by upgrading the position of the **Governor of Bengal** to the **Governor-General of Bengal**, who was assisted by a council consisting of four members. *Hence, the correct option is stated.*
 
• The Governor-General of Bengal was given supervisory authority over the presidencies of Bombay and Madras, centralizing the administration in India.
 
• The council was created to assist the Governor-General in decision-making, and decisions were subject to majority voting within the council.
 
• This Act aimed to curb corruption and mismanagement in the East India Company's administration in India. *Hence, this administrative change was significant.*
 
• The Act also introduced provisions for the appointment of a Chief Justice and judges in Calcutta, establishing the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of the Regulating Act:**

 
 
• The primary purpose of the Act was to address **administrative inefficiencies** and **corruption** within the East India Company.
 
• It sought to establish a centralized form of governance by placing the **Governor-General of Bengal** at the helm of administration and limiting the powers of other presidencies like Madras and Bombay.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor-General:**
 
 
• The Governor-General of Bengal became the central figure in British India's administration, with **Warren Hastings** serving as the first Governor-General under the Act.
 
• The council, consisting of four members, was created to assist the Governor-General in decision-making processes, which ensured administrative accountability.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Provisions:**
 
 
• The Act established the **Supreme Court of Judicature** at Fort William in Calcutta, marking the beginning of a formal judicial system in British India.
 
• The Supreme Court had jurisdiction over civil, criminal, and revenue matters within the region of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of the Regulating Act:**

 
 
• The Act was the first legal framework to regulate the affairs of the East India Company and ensured that the company operated under the supervision of the British Parliament.
 
• The appointment of the Governor-General and council members required approval from the British Crown, ensuring **direct accountability** to the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Act:**
 
 
• It laid the foundation for centralization in Indian administration and marked the beginning of a structured governance system.
 
• The Act also established the principle of separation of powers by introducing judicial oversight through the Supreme Court.
